COMPENSATION DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

This section explains how we paid our named executive officers for fiscal 2025 and why. Our named executive officers were Nadia Oyelaran, Chief Executive Officer; Ivo Brandsma, Chief Financial Officer; Priyanka Deshmukh, Chief Technology Officer; Colm Brennan, Chief People Officer; and Marguerite Vance, General Counsel.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Fiscal 2025 revenue grew 19% and free cash flow turned positive for the first time. Against that, the Compensation Committee funded the annual bonus at 112% of target and granted the equity mix described below. The Committee made no upward discretionary adjustment to any named executive officer's bonus.

SAY-ON-PAY

At our 2025 annual meeting, 94.1% of the votes cast supported our executive compensation. The Committee considered that result and made no change to the program's design in response. We hold the say-on-pay vote annually, as our stockholders directed at the 2023 meeting.

HOW PAY IS SET

The Committee retains Halvard Compensation Partners as its independent adviser. The Committee assessed the adviser's independence under Nasdaq Rule 5605(d)(3) and the six factors in Rule 10C-1 and identified no conflict of interest. Management proposes goals; the Committee sets them, assesses performance, and approves pay for every named executive officer. The Chief Executive Officer is not present when her own pay is decided.

Our peer group is fifteen companies of comparable revenue and market capitalization in optical components and instrumentation. The Committee reviews the group annually and removed two companies this year following their acquisition.

THE ELEMENTS

Base salary. Set on scope, experience, and market. The Committee increased base salaries by 3.5% on average in 2025.

Annual incentive. Target opportunity is 100% of salary for the CEO and 60% for the other named executive officers. For 2025 the plan weighted revenue 50%, free cash flow 30%, and three operating objectives 20%. Payout ranges from 0% to 200% of target, with no payout below a threshold of 90% of the revenue goal. Revenue finished at 104% of goal and free cash flow at 118%, producing a funded pool of 112%.

Long-term incentive. Sixty percent of the grant-date value is performance stock units earned on three-year relative total shareholder return against the peer group, capped at target if absolute TSR is negative; forty percent is time-vested restricted stock units vesting over four years.

COMPENSATION RISK

The Committee reviewed the program with management and the adviser and concluded that it does not create risk reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on the Company, because pay is balanced between short and long term, incentive plans are capped, goals are set at the corporate level, and the clawback and stock-ownership policies apply.

CLAWBACK

We maintain a compensation recovery policy that complies with Rule 10D-1 and Nasdaq Rule 5608. If we are required to prepare an accounting restatement, we will recover the incentive compensation received by a current or former executive officer during the three completed fiscal years before the restatement date that exceeds what would have been paid under the restated results, without regard to fault.

STOCK OWNERSHIP AND HEDGING

The Chief Executive Officer must hold shares worth six times base salary and the other named executive officers three times, within five years of appointment. Hedging and pledging of Company securities are prohibited, as described in our Insider Trading Policy.

PERQUISITES AND SEVERANCE

We provide no perquisites other than those available to employees generally. Severance on a qualifying termination is one times salary and target bonus for the CEO and 0.75 times for the other named executive officers, doubled on a qualifying termination within twenty-four months after a change in control. No agreement provides an excise-tax gross-up.

PAY RATIO

The annual total compensation of our median employee was $148,300 and of our Chief Executive Officer was $6,204,500, a ratio of 42 to 1. We identified the median employee using total cash compensation for all employees as of October 31, 2025, and calculated that employee's annual total compensation using the same rules that apply to the Summary Compensation Table.

COMPENSATION COMMITTEE REPORT

The Compensation Committee has reviewed and discussed this Compensation Discussion and Analysis with management and, based on that review and discussion, recommended to the Board that it be included in this proxy statement.

Submitted by the Compensation Committee: Rosalind Achebe (Chair), Emil Halloran, and Beatriz Salgado-Klein.
